h: A Shoreditch Day Built Around Your Game
p: Gamebox's games are designed to be replayed, with different rooms and themes on offer, so it's worth having a look at the current line-up before you book. The selection changes from time to time and has included games based on well-known films and TV shows alongside original adventures, so you can pick something to suit your gang, whether that's a family with young kids or a crowd of competitive mates.

Time it right and you can stitch together a cracking day in this part of East London. Spitalfields Market, a short walk south, is a covered Victorian market hall full of independent stalls, food traders and shops. If your visit lands on a Sunday, the Columbia Road Flower Market is a riot of colour and noise, with traders shouting their deals on bunches of blooms.

For culture, the Museum of the Home on Kingsland Road takes you through centuries of how Londoners have lived, with recreated rooms and gardens, and it's free to visit. Street art fans can spend hours wandering the backstreets around Shoreditch High Street, where the walls are constantly changing with new murals and paste-ups.

Food-wise you're spoilt. Boxpark Shoreditch, made from shipping containers, is packed with street food stalls and bars, and the curry houses and bagel bakeries of Brick Lane are just round the corner, with the bagel shops famous for being open around the clock. Getting there is easy too, with Shoreditch High Street Overground station right in the middle of things and Liverpool Street and Old Street both a short walk away. It's a perfect patch of London for an afternoon that runs into the evening.
